chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, raising it (marfu'), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) heard a man saying, 'I disavow the religion of Muhammad.' So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: 'Woe to you! If you disavow the religion of Muhammad, then upon whose religion will you be?' He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did not speak to him until he died.

key_terms.بَرِيء: Disavowal, free from, not responsible for — used in legal oaths and expressions of separation
key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: He raised it (marfu') — a technical hadith term indicating the chain is elevated to the Prophet without naming all intermediate transmitters
key_terms.وَيْل: Woe, destruction — a Quranic exclamation expressing dismay at someone's dire state

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad do when he heard a man disavow his religion?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Ali ibn Ibrahim via a marfu' (elevated) narration, recounts an incident where a man rashly declared his disavowal of the Prophet Muhammad's religion — likely in the context of an oath or argument. The Prophet's sharp rhetorical question, 'Whose religion will you be upon?', exposes the absurdity of such a declaration, and his subsequent silence towards the man until his death reflects the gravity of apostasy and the severing of bonds in Islamic law and social custom. The chapter context indicates this hadith addresses the abhorrence of swearing oaths by disavowing God or the Prophet.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, raising it, said, ‘Rasool-Allah

saww heard a man saying, ‘I disavow from the Religion of Muhammadsaww’. So Rasool-Allahsaww said to him: ‘Woe be unto you! When you disavow from the Religion of Muhammadsaww, so upon whose Religion would you happen to be?’ Heasws said: ‘So Rasool-Allahsaww had not spoken to him, until (immediately) he died’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from in a marfu‘ manner who has narrated the following: “

The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, once heard a man saying, T disown the religion of Muhammad.’ The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, then asked saying, ‘Woe is upon you, if you are not a follower of the religion of Muhammad, then whose religion do you follow?’ He (the Imam) has said that as soon as the words of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, were complete, he (the man) dropped dead.’”
